summary: The article offers strategies and three recipes for feeding picky eaters, drawing on a pediatric dietitian, a family, a home cook, and a chef. Its main advice is to expose kids to varied foods without pressure, involve them in cooking, use natural sweetness, and disguise vegetables in fun shapes or blended sauces. Full ingredient lists and directions are given for a pasta bake, a frozen yogurt, and cauliflower tots.
one_line: Expert tips and three recipes (veggie pasta bake, banana berry frozen yogurt, cauliflower tots) for getting picky kids to eat nutritious food.
key_facts: Dr. Angela Pearson, a pediatric dietitian, was interviewed on October 12th, 2023 and said picky eating is "a mixture of control, fear of the new, and a developing palette."
Dr. Pearson recommends exposing children to a variety of foods in a non-pressure environment and making it enjoyable.
Pressuring children to try new foods can lead to power struggles that worsen picky habits.
Lisa and Mark Thompson say involvement is their key to success: "We make cooking a family affair." Their twins, Ella and Max, help wash vegetables and mix ingredients.
The Thompsons' Veggie-Packed Tomato Pasta Bake blends bell pepper, zucchini, spinach, onion and garlic into the tomato sauce, and is baked at 375°F (190°C) for about 20 minutes.
The pasta bake uses 2 cups of whole-grain pasta, 2 cups of tomato sauce, 1 cup of low-fat mozzarella and 1/4 cup of parmesan; Mark Thompson says leftovers are great for lunchboxes.
Melissa Sanders, a mother of three and amateur chef, uses fruits and natural sweeteners to limit sugar in her kids' desserts.
Sanders' Homemade Banana Berry Frozen Yogurt uses 2 frozen ripe bananas, 1 cup of frozen mixed berries, 1/2 cup of Greek yogurt and an optional tablespoon of honey, blended in a food processor.
The frozen yogurt can be served immediately for soft-serve consistency or frozen about an hour for a firmer texture.
Chef James Robertson, known for kid-friendly menus, was interviewed on November 20th, 2023 and says turning nutritious food into fun, bite-size shapes encourages kids to try new things.

Robertson's Cheesy Cauliflower Tots use 2 cups of cauliflower florets, 1 egg, 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs and 1/2 cup of shredded cheese, and are baked at 400°F (200°C) for about 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
The tots are served with ketchup or the child's favorite dipping sauce; Robertson says even vegetable-averse kids get excited about them.
